LESSON: WRITING 15.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.4: Writing 15.4.1 Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 15.4.1 Guided Writing, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we prepare for writing? 2) What makes it easy to write a good sentence?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. point out the different punctuation marks used in a variety of sentences.

2. punctuate sentences correctly.

3. practise writing short sentences related to the theme from a substitution table.

4. respond to picture prompts/picture descriptions and write sentences (not more than 7 words) related to the theme 1)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. point out the different punctuation marks used in a variety of sentences.
2. punctuate sentences correctly.
3. practise writing short sentences related to the theme from a substitution table.
4. respond to picture prompts/picture descriptions and write sentences (not more than 7 words) related to the theme 1)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 15.4.1 Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn-as learners practise writing sentences from varied prompts

Values:
Respect as a learner works with peers in groups or pairs and appreciates different views from peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (effective communication) as learner develops independent writing skills.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages Activities develop independent writing skills
